chapter: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
title: Floyd Turner and his musical family from Spokane
summary: The Howards recall Floyd Turner coming from Spokane around 1931 with parents who ran a big band.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: What about Floyd Turner?
Now, Floyd, I don't know too much about him.
Floyd came out here in -- let me see, was it '30? '31.
Don't know too much about Floyd.
But isn't he from, like, the whole family --
He's from Spokane. Yes, --
(Unintelligible), because I remember the mother, the father, --
Yeah. Yeah, the father and the mother, the father and the mother playing drums and playing piano. Piano and drums.
His mother was on piano, father was on drums.
It was like a trio? Just the three of them?
No, no, no, they had a big band.
Oh, they did.
Yes.
Yeah, they had a big band.
Because I knew Floyd. I knew the family in Spokane, see, and -- because Edith played out at a roadhouse there, on Wednesday nights when the band had a night off. Now, she had a good band.
and, you know, I never heard the band.
I heard about it and everything.

She did, uh-huh. Really, she had a good band. And they came out here, oh, I believe it was around '31, '32, somewhere. I believe it was -- I can't remember the time, but nevertheless, Floyd was just a youngster then, but he was playing sax, he was playing in the band.
Yeah, uh-huh.
There's not much more to do — or hing.
